title: Homes Hill
summary: Homes Hill is recorded as a hill at North Sea in Southampton.
address_label: Homes Hill / North Sea Harbor, Southampton, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate general marker based on Tooker identifying Homes as a hill at North Sea and local history placing Homes Hill above North Sea Harbor near Conscience Point.
translation_content:
Homes is connected with a Narragansett word meaning an old man. He presents the name as likely marking a place associated with an older Native resident, while noting that the term carried respect for age rather than a sense of frailty.

Whomeses is kept as an early or related form cross-referenced to Homes.

Why Place Names Matter

“When Indigenous Peoples reclaim their place names and re-inscribe them on map and memory, they take a bold step toward self-determination and the preservation of their biocultural heritage.”

— Terralingua, What’s in an Indigenous Place Name? (2024), opening statement
land_loss_content: Homes Hill keeps a personal and landscape memory attached to North Sea, where colonial records preserved a Native-language term through changing spellings. Recording the uncertainty helps protect the place reference without overstating what the records prove.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for the Homes Hill / North Sea Harbor landscape near Conscience Point, not an exact surveyed hilltop coordinate.
